To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of Tra-2β mRNA was enhanced in motoneurons following hypoglossal axotomy and in the brain following brain injury, and that the up-regulation of the Tra-2β was correlated with the expression of regeneration-associated molecules.
Tra2beta mRNA is up-regulated transiently in response to injury of motoneurons and that the up-regulation of the Tra2beta mRNA may participate in injury-specific splicing pattern in motoneurons.
Tra2beta mRNA is up-regulated transiently in injured motoneuron and that this up-regulation is induced by nerve injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of Tra-2beta in the motoneurons after nerve injury.
the role of splicing in the regulation of gene expression in the injured nervous system.
the expression of Tra proteins in the nervous system, and the possible role of Tra2beta in the control of mRNA splicing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the up-regulation of the Tra2beta gene in response to nerve lesion may be a part of a cellular response to nerve damage.
Tra2beta is a sequence-specific splicing factor which is induced in injured motoneuron and that Tra2beta plays an important role in the control of mRNA splicing in response to injury.
Tra2beta plays important roles in nerve regeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the splicing factor Tra2beta is involved in nerve injury-induced alternative splicing in neurons.
the up-regulation of the splicing activator in injured neurons may be involved in the regulation of the splicing patterns of mRNA, which is necessary for the regeneration of injured axons.
Tra2beta is a key regulator for the injury-specific splicing pattern of the mRNA encoding for a regeneration-associated molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Tra2β protein is up-regulated after injury and that the up-regulation is transient.
Tra2beta, a sequence-specific splicing factor, is a novel factor in nerve injury-induced alternative splicing.
Tra2beta is upregulated after peripheral nerve injury and brain injury, which may be involved in injury-specific splicing pattern.
